title: Add Closed Hover Micro Animations to Every Icon
description: Add a hover-triggered micro animation to every icon in the UI. Trigger on hovering the icon itself or its enclosing interactive control (button, link, menu item, tab, etc.). Play once per hover-enter. Every animation must be closed: first keyframe equals last keyframe (rest -> motion -> identical rest), so it ends seamlessly and is loopable. Give every one of the 144 vendored Lucide icons (plus 10 more to be vendored: app-window, square-dashed, redo-2, undo-2, edit-3, align-left, list-ordered, text-cursor, clipboard, file) a bespoke, semantically fitting closed keyframe animation, keyed off the existing data-icon attribute on the central Icon component (ui/js/react/index.tsx). Also add data-icon-kind to non-catalog icon kinds (emoji, text, typst, url/data image, raw svg, node, missing-placeholder) with their own closed animations so literally every icon animates. Remap the non-Lucide "glb" icon id to the vendored "box" icon via an alias. Extend ui.css with the keyframes, a single generic hover-trigger rule, and a prefers-reduced-motion guard. Extend the in-source vitest tests in ui/js/react/index.tsx to assert completeness (every icon id has a keyframes block + assignment) and closed-ness (0% frame equals 100% frame, except declared full-turn spin exceptions ending at +/-360deg). Extend the Icons storybook story with a hover-animation demo grid.
summary:
Second follow-up per user feedback: "Make every single one 100% specific. e.g. the settings icon should move the knobs."

Extended real per-part mechanism animations from the initial 27 icons to 122 of the 154 vendored icons total — every icon whose SVG has cleanly separable moving parts, verified against the actual committed SVG source in `ui/asset/icon/*.svg`. Examples from this pass: bell's body swings on its pivot while the clapper lags behind with its own phase-delayed swing; calendar-days' day-dots pulse in a left-to-right wave and the binding rings lift; square-dashed's 12 border dashes do a "marching ants" opacity chase around the perimeter; sun's rays shimmer independently while the disc glows; home's door swings open on its hinge; hand's three fingers wiggle with a stagger (waving); users/component/network nodes pulse to show data/people connecting; layout-grid's four quadrants nudge toward/away from center; file-code/file-json/code's bracket glyphs open apart; scaling/external-link/maximize-2's resize handles pull apart along the diagonal; eye's eyelid and pupil animate as two distinct layers; and so on for the rest (full per-icon list and rationale in the CSS comments).

Notably, the user's own example — "settings icon should move the knobs" — actually names `settings-2` (the slider icon), which already got real sliding knobs in the *first* follow-up pass; `settings` (the gear) intentionally keeps its whole-icon full rotation, since a gear spinning as one rigid piece *is* the mechanically correct motion, not an approximation. The same reasoning applies to `globe`, `search`, `rotate-cw/ccw`, and `text-cursor` (a blinking cursor is already exactly right) — these 5 (plus `settings`) were deliberately left as whole-icon rigid motion rather than artificially split.

Caught and fixed one over-eager mistake during this pass: `flip-horizontal`/`flip-vertical` were briefly converted to a "brackets tug apart" per-part motion, but a full rotateY/rotateX flip of the *entire* icon is actually the more literal and correct representation of "flip" — reverted those two back to their original whole-icon full-turn spin (removing the now-orphaned per-part keyframes) before finalizing.

The remaining 30 icons split into: 24 with a single fused SVG path (chevrons, check, x-shapes like triangle/circle/square/hexagon, moon, cloud, filter, folder, folder-open, play, puzzle, wrench, sigma, table-2, message-circle/square, minus, mouse-pointer-2, loader-2) where no sub-part exists without redrawing the vendored SVG — out of scope for a CSS-only pass — and the 6 "already mechanically correct" ones named above.

Architecture: reused the exact same generic per-part CSS engine from the first pass (12 nth-child slots driven by `--icon-part-<N>-anim/-origin/-duration` custom properties). Added ~90 new bespoke `@keyframes` across two generator passes (heavy reuse of shared primitives like `icon-commit-dot` for "pulse" cues and `icon-crosshair-{top,bottom,left,right}` for directional nudges, applied with different origins/durations per icon). All verified closed (0% === 100%) programmatically before writing, with zero keyframe-name collisions and zero unresolved animation references checked across the whole file.

Updated the in-source vitest completeness test's `PART_MECHANISM_ICONS` set to the full, file-verified 122-icon list, and relaxed the closedness test's total-keyframe-count sanity check (it no longer scales 1:1 with icon count now that dozens of icons share reusable part-keyframes). All 7 icon tests pass; `framework-renderer-react` regression suite passes in full (239/239).
